name: exercise_2_2_9
natural_language_statement: Let $H$ be the subgroup generated by two elements $a, b$ of a group $G$. Prove that if $a b=b a$, then $H$ is an abelian group.

name: exercise_2_3_2
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Group G] (a b : G) :
  ∃ g : G, b* a = g * a * b * g⁻¹ :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that the products $a b$ and $b a$ are conjugate elements in a group.

name: exercise_2_4_19
natural_language_statement: Prove that if a group contains exactly one element of order 2 , then that element is in the center of the group.

name: exercise_2_8_6
formal_statement:
{G H : Type*} [Group G] [Group H] :
  center (G × H) ≃* (center G) × (center H) :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that the center of the product of two groups is the product of their centers.

name: exercise_2_11_3
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G]
  (hG : Even (card G)) : ∃ x : G, orderOf x = 2 :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that a group of even order contains an element of order $2 .$

name: exercise_3_2_7
formal_statement:
{F : Type*} [Field F] {G : Type*} [Field G]
  (φ : F →+* G) : Injective φ :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that every homomorphism of fields is injective.

name: exercise_3_5_6
formal_statement:
{K V : Type*} [Field K] [AddCommGroup V]
  [Module K V] {S : Set V} (hS : Set.Countable S)
  (hS1 : span K S = ⊤) {ι : Type*} (R : ι → V)
  (hR : LinearIndependent K R) : Countable ι :=
natural_language_statement: Let $V$ be a vector space which is spanned by a countably infinite set. Prove that every linearly independent subset of $V$ is finite or countably infinite.

name: exercise_3_7_2
formal_statement:
{K V : Type*} [Field K] [AddCommGroup V]
  [Module K V] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (γ : ι → Submodule K V)
  (h : ∀ i : ι, γ i ≠ ⊤) :
  (⋂ (i : ι), (γ i : Set V)) ≠ ⊤ :=
natural_language_statement: Let $V$ be a vector space over an infinite field $F$. Prove that $V$ is not the union of finitely many proper subspaces.

name: exercise_6_1_14
formal_statement:
(G : Type*) [Group G]
  (hG : IsCyclic $ G ⧸ (center G)) :hju
  center G = ⊤  :=
natural_language_statement: Let $Z$ be the center of a group $G$. Prove that if $G / Z$ is a cyclic group, then $G$ is abelian and hence $G=Z$.

name: exercise_6_4_2
natural_language_statement: Prove that no group of order $p q$, where $p$ and $q$ are prime, is simple.

name: exercise_6_4_3
natural_language_statement: Prove that no group of order $p^2 q$, where $p$ and $q$ are prime, is simple.

name: exercise_6_4_12
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G]
  (hG : card G = 224) :
  IsSimpleGroup G → false :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that no group of order 224 is simple.

name: exercise_6_8_1
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Group G]
  (a b : G) : closure ({a, b} : Set G) = Subgroup.closure {b*a*b^2, b*a*b^3} :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that two elements $a, b$ of a group generate the same subgroup as $b a b^2, b a b^3$.

name: exercise_10_1_13
formal_statement:
{R : Type*} [Ring R] {x : R}
  (hx : IsNilpotent x) : IsUnit (1 + x) :=
natural_language_statement: An element $x$ of a ring $R$ is called nilpotent if some power of $x$ is zero. Prove that if $x$ is nilpotent, then $1+x$ is a unit in $R$.

name: exercise_10_2_4
formal_statement:
:
  span ({2} : Set $ Polynomial ℤ) ⊓ (span {X}) =
  span ({2 * X} : Set $ Polynomial ℤ) :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that in the ring $\mathbb{Z}[x],(2) \cap(x)=(2 x)$.

name: exercise_10_6_7
formal_statement:
{I : Ideal GaussianInt}
  (hI : I ≠ ⊥) : ∃ (z : I), z ≠ 0 ∧ (z : GaussianInt).im = 0 :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that every nonzero ideal in the ring of Gauss integers contains a nonzero integer.

name: exercise_10_4_6
formal_statement:
{R : Type*} [CommRing R]
  [NoZeroDivisors R] (I J : Ideal R) (x : ↑(I ⊓ J)) :
  IsNilpotent ((Ideal.Quotient.mk (I*J)) x) :=
natural_language_statement: Let $I, J$ be ideals in a ring $R$. Prove that the residue of any element of $I \cap J$ in $R / I J$ is nilpotent.

name: exercise_10_4_7a
formal_statement:
{R : Type*} [CommRing R] [NoZeroDivisors R]
  (I J : Ideal R) (hIJ : I + J = ⊤) : I * J = I ⊓ J :=
natural_language_statement: Let $I, J$ be ideals of a ring $R$ such that $I+J=R$. Prove that $I J=I \cap J$.

name: exercise_10_7_10
formal_statement:
{R : Type*} [Ring R]
  (M : Ideal R) (hM : ∀ (x : R), x ∉ M → IsUnit x)
  (hProper : ∃ x : R, x ∉ M) :
  IsMaximal M ∧ ∀ (N : Ideal R), IsMaximal N → N = M :=
natural_language_statement: Let $R$ be a ring, with $M$ an ideal of $R$. Suppose that every element of $R$ which is not in $M$ is a unit of $R$. Prove that $M$ is a maximal ideal and that moreover it is the only maximal ideal of $R$.

name: exercise_11_2_13
formal_statement:
(a b : ℤ) :
  (ofInt a : GaussianInt) ∣ ofInt b → a ∣ b :=
natural_language_statement: If $a, b$ are integers and if $a$ divides $b$ in the ring of Gauss integers, then $a$ divides $b$ in $\mathbb{Z}$.

name: exercise_11_4_1b
formal_statement:
{F : Type*} [Field F] [Fintype F] (hF : card F = 2) :
  Irreducible (12 + 6 * X + X ^ 3 : Polynomial F) :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that $x^3 + 6x + 12$ is irreducible in $\mathbb{Q}$.

name: exercise_11_4_6a
formal_statement:
{F : Type*} [Field F] [Fintype F] (hF : card F = 7) :
  Irreducible (X ^ 2 + 1 : Polynomial F) :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that $x^2+x+1$ is irreducible in the field $\mathbb{F}_2$.

name: exercise_11_4_6b
formal_statement:
{F : Type*} [Field F] [Fintype F] (hF : card F = 31) :
  Irreducible (X ^ 3 - 9 : Polynomial F) :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that $x^2+1$ is irreducible in $\mathbb{F}_7$

name: exercise_11_4_6c
formal_statement: : Irreducible (X^3 - 9 : Polynomial (ZMod 31)) :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that $x^3 - 9$ is irreducible in $\mathbb{F}_{31}$.

name: exercise_11_4_8
formal_statement:
(p : ℕ) (hp : Prime p) (n : ℕ) :
  -- p ∈ ℕ can be written as p ∈ ℚ[X]
  Irreducible (X ^ n - (p : Polynomial ℚ) : Polynomial ℚ) :=
natural_language_statement: Let $p$ be a prime integer. Prove that the polynomial $x^n-p$ is irreducible in $\mathbb{Q}[x]$.

name: exercise_11_13_3
formal_statement:
(N : ℕ):
  ∃ p ≥ N, Nat.Prime p ∧ p + 1 ≡ 0 [MOD 4] :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that there are infinitely many primes congruent to $-1$ (modulo $4$).

name: exercise_13_4_10
natural_language_statement: Prove that if a prime integer $p$ has the form $2^r+1$, then it actually has the form $2^{2^k}+1$.

name: exercise_13_6_10
formal_statement:
{K : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype Kˣ] :
  (∏ x : Kˣ,  x) = -1 :=
natural_language_statement: Let $K$ be a finite field. Prove that the product of the nonzero elements of $K$ is $-1$.

name: exercise_1_2
natural_language_statement: Show that $\frac{-1 + \sqrt{3}i}{2}$ is a cube root of 1 (meaning that its cube equals 1).

name: exercise_1_3
formal_statement:
{F V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Field F]
  [Module F V] {v : V} : -(-v) = v :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that $-(-v) = v$ for every $v \in V$.

name: exercise_1_4
formal_statement:
{F V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Field F]
  [Module F V] (v : V) (a : F): a • v = 0 ↔ a = 0 ∨ v = 0 :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that if $a \in \mathbf{F}$, $v \in V$, and $av = 0$, then $a = 0$ or $v = 0$.

name: exercise_1_6
formal_statement:
: ∃ U : Set (ℝ × ℝ),
  (U ≠ ∅) ∧
  (∀ (u v : ℝ × ℝ), u ∈ U ∧ v ∈ U → u + v ∈ U) ∧
  (∀ (u : ℝ × ℝ), u ∈ U → -u ∈ U) ∧
  (∀ U' : Submodule ℝ (ℝ × ℝ), U ≠ ↑U') :=
natural_language_statement: Give an example of a nonempty subset $U$ of $\mathbf{R}^2$ such that $U$ is closed under addition and under taking additive inverses (meaning $-u \in U$ whenever $u \in U$), but $U$ is not a subspace of $\mathbf{R}^2$.

name: exercise_1_7
formal_statement:
: ∃ U : Set (ℝ × ℝ),
  (U ≠ ∅) ∧
  (∀ (c : ℝ) (u : ℝ × ℝ), u ∈ U → c • u ∈ U) ∧
  (∀ U' : Submodule ℝ (ℝ × ℝ), U ≠ ↑U') :=
natural_language_statement: Give an example of a nonempty subset $U$ of $\mathbf{R}^2$ such that $U$ is closed under scalar multiplication, but $U$ is not a subspace of $\mathbf{R}^2$.

name: exercise_1_8
formal_statement:
{F V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Field F]
  [Module F V] {ι : Type*} (u : ι → Submodule F V) :
  ∃ U : Submodule F V, (⋂ (i : ι), (u i).carrier) = ↑U :=
  by
natural_language_statement: Prove that the intersection of any collection of subspaces of $V$ is a subspace of $V$.

name: exercise_1_9
formal_statement:
{F V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Field F]
  [Module F V] (U W : Submodule F V):
  ∃ U' : Submodule F V, (U'.carrier = ↑U ∩ ↑W ↔ (U ≤ W ∨ W ≤ U)) :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that the union of two subspaces of $V$ is a subspace of $V$ if and only if one of the subspaces is contained in the other.

name: exercise_3_1
formal_statement:
{F V : Type*}
  [AddCommGroup V] [Field F] [Module F V] [FiniteDimensional F V]
  (T : V →ₗ[F] V) (hT : finrank F V = 1) :
  ∃ c : F, ∀ v : V, T v = c • v:=
natural_language_statement: Show that every linear map from a one-dimensional vector space to itself is multiplication by some scalar. More precisely, prove that if $\operatorname{dim} V=1$ and $T \in \mathcal{L}(V, V)$, then there exists $a \in \mathbf{F}$ such that $T v=a v$ for all $v \in V$.

name: exercise_3_8
formal_statement:
{F V W : Type*}  [AddCommGroup V]
  [AddCommGroup W] [Field F] [Module F V] [Module F W]
  (L : V →ₗ[F] W) :
  ∃ U : Submodule F V, U ⊓ (ker L) = ⊥ ∧
  (range L = range (domRestrict L U)):=
natural_language_statement: Suppose that $V$ is finite dimensional and that $T \in \mathcal{L}(V, W)$. Prove that there exists a subspace $U$ of $V$ such that $U \cap \operatorname{null} T=\{0\}$ and range $T=\{T u: u \in U\}$.

name: exercise_4_4
formal_statement:
(p : Polynomial ℂ) :
  p.degree = @card (rootSet p ℂ) (rootSetFintype p ℂ) ↔
  Disjoint
  (@card (rootSet (derivative p) ℂ) (rootSetFintype (derivative p) ℂ))
  (@card (rootSet p ℂ) (rootSetFintype p ℂ)) :=
natural_language_statement: Suppose $p \in \mathcal{P}(\mathbf{C})$ has degree $m$. Prove that $p$ has $m$ distinct roots if and only if $p$ and its derivative $p^{\prime}$ have no roots in common.

name: exercise_5_1
formal_statement:
{F V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Field F]
  [Module F V] {L : V →ₗ[F] V} {n : ℕ} (U : Fin n → Submodule F V)
  (hU : ∀ i : Fin n, Submodule.map L (U i) = U i) :
  Submodule.map L (∑ i : Fin n, U i : Submodule F V) =
  (∑ i : Fin n, U i : Submodule F V) :=
natural_language_statement: Suppose $T \in \mathcal{L}(V)$. Prove that if $U_{1}, \ldots, U_{m}$ are subspaces of $V$ invariant under $T$, then $U_{1}+\cdots+U_{m}$ is invariant under $T$.

name: exercise_5_4
formal_statement:
{F V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Field F]
  [Module F V] (S T : V →ₗ[F] V) (hST : S ∘ T = T ∘ S) (c : F):
  Submodule.map S (ker (T - c • LinearMap.id)) = ker (T - c • LinearMap.id) :=
natural_language_statement: Suppose that $S, T \in \mathcal{L}(V)$ are such that $S T=T S$. Prove that $\operatorname{null} (T-\lambda I)$ is invariant under $S$ for every $\lambda \in \mathbf{F}$.

name: exercise_5_11
formal_statement:
{F V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Field F]
  [Module F V] (S T : End F V) :
  (S * T).Eigenvalues = (T * S).Eigenvalues :=
natural_language_statement: Suppose $S, T \in \mathcal{L}(V)$. Prove that $S T$ and $T S$ have the same eigenvalues.

name: exercise_5_12
formal_statement:
{F V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Field F]
  [Module F V] {S : End F V}
  (hS : ∀ v : V, ∃ c : F, v ∈ eigenspace S c) :
  ∃ c : F, S = c • LinearMap.id :=
natural_language_statement: Suppose $T \in \mathcal{L}(V)$ is such that every vector in $V$ is an eigenvector of $T$. Prove that $T$ is a scalar multiple of the identity operator.

name: exercise_5_13
formal_statement:
{F V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Field F]
  [Module F V] [FiniteDimensional F V] {T : End F V}
  (hS : ∀ U : Submodule F V, finrank F U = finrank F V - 1 →
  Submodule.map T U = U) : ∃ c : F, T = c • LinearMap.id :=
natural_language_statement: Suppose $T \in \mathcal{L}(V)$ is such that every subspace of $V$ with dimension $\operatorname{dim} V-1$ is invariant under $T$. Prove that $T$ is a scalar multiple of the identity operator.

name: exercise_5_20
formal_statement:
{F V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Field F]
  [Module F V] [FiniteDimensional F V] {S T : End F V}
  (h1 : card (T.Eigenvalues) = finrank F V)
  (h2 : ∀ v : V, ∃ c : F, v ∈ eigenspace S c ↔ ∃ c : F, v ∈ eigenspace T c) :
  S * T = T * S :=
natural_language_statement: Suppose that $T \in \mathcal{L}(V)$ has $\operatorname{dim} V$ distinct eigenvalues and that $S \in \mathcal{L}(V)$ has the same eigenvectors as $T$ (not necessarily with the same eigenvalues). Prove that $S T=T S$.

name: exercise_5_24
natural_language_statement: Suppose $V$ is a real vector space and $T \in \mathcal{L}(V)$ has no eigenvalues. Prove that every subspace of $V$ invariant under $T$ has even dimension.

name: exercise_6_2
formal_statement:
{V : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
[InnerProductSpace ℂ V] (u v : V) :
  ⟪u, v⟫_ℂ = 0 ↔ ∀ (a : ℂ), ‖u‖  ≤ ‖u + a • v‖ :=
natural_language_statement: Suppose $u, v \in V$. Prove that $\langle u, v\rangle=0$ if and only if $\|u\| \leq\|u+a v\|$ for all $a \in \mathbf{F}$.

name: exercise_6_3
formal_statement:
{n : ℕ} (a b : Fin n → ℝ) :
  (∑ i, a i * b i) ^ 2 ≤ (∑ i : Fin n, i * a i ^ 2) * (∑ i, b i ^ 2 / i) :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that $\left(\sum_{j=1}^{n} a_{j} b_{j}\right)^{2} \leq\left(\sum_{j=1}^{n} j a_{j}{ }^{2}\right)\left(\sum_{j=1}^{n} \frac{b_{j}{ }^{2}}{j}\right)$ for all real numbers $a_{1}, \ldots, a_{n}$ and $b_{1}, \ldots, b_{n}$.

name: exercise_6_7
formal_statement:
{V : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℂ V] (u v : V) :
  ⟪u, v⟫_ℂ = (‖u + v‖^2 - ‖u - v‖^2 + I*‖u + I•v‖^2 - I*‖u-I•v‖^2) / 4 :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that if $V$ is a complex inner-product space, then $\langle u, v\rangle=\frac{\|u+v\|^{2}-\|u-v\|^{2}+\|u+i v\|^{2} i-\|u-i v\|^{2} i}{4}$ for all $u, v \in V$.

name: exercise_6_13
natural_language_statement: Suppose $\left(e_{1}, \ldots, e_{m}\right)$ is an orthonormal list of vectors in $V$. Let $v \in V$. Prove that $\|v\|^{2}=\left|\left\langle v, e_{1}\right\rangle\right|^{2}+\cdots+\left|\left\langle v, e_{m}\right\rangle\right|^{2}$ if and only if $v \in \operatorname{span}\left(e_{1}, \ldots, e_{m}\right)$.

name: exercise_6_16
formal_statement:
{K V : Type*} [IsROrC K] [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace K V]
  {U : Submodule K V} :
  U.orthogonal = ⊥  ↔ U = ⊤ :=
natural_language_statement: Suppose $U$ is a subspace of $V$. Prove that $U^{\perp}=\{0\}$ if and only if $U=V$

name: exercise_7_5
formal_statement:
{V : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℂ V]
  [FiniteDimensional ℂ V] (hV : finrank V ≥ 2) :
  ∀ U : Submodule ℂ (End ℂ V), U.carrier ≠
  {T | T * adjoint T = adjoint T * T} :=
natural_language_statement: Show that if $\operatorname{dim} V \geq 2$, then the set of normal operators on $V$ is not a subspace of $\mathcal{L}(V)$.

name: exercise_7_6
formal_statement:
{V : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℂ V]
  [FiniteDimensional ℂ V] (T : End ℂ V)
  (hT : T * adjoint T = adjoint T * T) :
  range T = range (adjoint T) :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that if $T \in \mathcal{L}(V)$ is normal, then $\operatorname{range} T=\operatorname{range} T^{*}.$

name: exercise_7_9
formal_statement:
{V : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℂ V]
  [FiniteDimensional ℂ V] (T : End ℂ V)
  (hT : T * adjoint T = adjoint T * T) :
  IsSelfAdjoint T ↔ ∀ e : T.Eigenvalues, (e : ℂ).im = 0 :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that a normal operator on a complex inner-product space is self-adjoint if and only if all its eigenvalues are real.

name: exercise_7_10
formal_statement:
{V : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℂ V]
  [FiniteDimensional ℂ V] (T : End ℂ V)
  (hT : T * adjoint T = adjoint T * T) (hT1 : T^9 = T^8) :
  IsSelfAdjoint T ∧ T^2 = T :=
natural_language_statement: Suppose $V$ is a complex inner-product space and $T \in \mathcal{L}(V)$ is a normal operator such that $T^{9}=T^{8}$. Prove that $T$ is self-adjoint and $T^{2}=T$.

name: exercise_7_11
formal_statement:
{V : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℂ V]
  [FiniteDimensional ℂ V] {T : End ℂ V} (hT : T*adjoint T = adjoint T*T) :
  ∃ (S : End ℂ V), S ^ 2 = T :=
natural_language_statement: Suppose $V$ is a complex inner-product space. Prove that every normal operator on $V$ has a square root. (An operator $S \in \mathcal{L}(V)$ is called a square root of $T \in \mathcal{L}(V)$ if $S^{2}=T$.)

name: exercise_7_14
formal_statement:
{𝕜 V : Type*} [IsROrC 𝕜] [NormedAddCommGroup V]
  [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 V] [FiniteDimensional 𝕜 V]
  {T : End 𝕜 V} (hT : IsSelfAdjoint T)
  {l : 𝕜} {ε : ℝ} (he : ε > 0) : ∃ v : V, ‖v‖= 1 ∧ (‖T v - l • v‖ < ε →
  (∃ l' : T.Eigenvalues, ‖l - l'‖ < ε)) :=
natural_language_statement: Suppose $T \in \mathcal{L}(V)$ is self-adjoint, $\lambda \in \mathbf{F}$, and $\epsilon>0$. Prove that if there exists $v \in V$ such that $\|v\|=1$ and $\|T v-\lambda v\|<\epsilon,$ then $T$ has an eigenvalue $\lambda^{\prime}$ such that $\left|\lambda-\lambda^{\prime}\right|<\epsilon$.

name: exercise_2022_IA_4_I_1E_a
natural_language_statement: Show that there are infinitely many primes of the form $3 n+2$ with $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

name: exercise_2022_IA_4_I_2D_a
natural_language_statement: Prove that $\sqrt[3]{2}+\sqrt[3]{3}$ is irrational.

name: exercise_2022_IB_3_II_13G_a_i
formal_statement:
(U : Set ℂ) (hU : IsOpen U)
  (hU1 : Nonempty U) (hU2 : IsConnected U) (f : ℕ → ℂ → ℂ) (f' : ℂ → ℂ)
  (hf : ∀ n : ℕ, DifferentiableOn ℂ (f n) U)
  (hf1 : ∀ X ⊂ U, CompactSpace X →
  (TendstoUniformly (λ n => restrict X (f n)) (restrict X f') atTop)) :
  DifferentiableOn ℂ f' U :=
natural_language_statement: Let $U \subset \mathbb{C}$ be a (non-empty) connected open set and let $f_n$ be a sequence of holomorphic functions defined on $U$. Suppose that $f_n$ converges uniformly to a function $f$ on every compact subset of $U$. Show that $f$ is holomorphic in $U$.

name: exercise_1_1_2a
formal_statement: : ∃ a b : ℤ, a - b ≠ b - a :=
natural_language_statement: Prove the the operation $\star$ on $\mathbb{Z}$ defined by $a\star b=a-b$ is not commutative.

name: exercise_1_1_3
formal_statement:
(n : ℤ) :
  ∀ (a b c : ℤ), (a+b)+c ≡ a+(b+c) [ZMOD n] :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that the addition of residue classes $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ is associative.

name: exercise_1_1_4
formal_statement:
(n : ℕ) :
  ∀ (a b c : ℕ), (a * b) * c ≡ a * (b * c) [ZMOD n] :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that the multiplication of residue class $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ is associative.

name: exercise_1_1_5
formal_statement:
(n : ℕ) (hn : 1 < n) :
  IsEmpty (Group (ZMod n)) :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that for all $n>1$ that $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ is not a group under multiplication of residue classes.

name: exercise_1_1_15
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Group G] (as : List G) :
  as.prod⁻¹ = (as.reverse.map (λ x => x⁻¹)).prod :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that $(a_1a_2\dots a_n)^{-1} = a_n^{-1}a_{n-1}^{-1}\dots a_1^{-1}$ for all $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n\in G$.

name: exercise_1_1_16
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Group G]
  (x : G) (hx : x ^ 2 = 1) :
  orderOf x = 1 ∨ orderOf x = 2 :=
natural_language_statement: Let $x$ be an element of $G$. Prove that $x^2=1$ if and only if $|x|$ is either $1$ or $2$.

name: exercise_1_1_17
natural_language_statement: Let $x$ be an element of $G$. Prove that if $|x|=n$ for some positive integer $n$ then $x^{-1}=x^{n-1}$.

name: exercise_1_1_18
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Group G]
  (x y : G) : (x * y = y * x ↔ y⁻¹ * x * y = x) ↔ (x⁻¹ * y⁻¹ * x * y = 1) :=
natural_language_statement: Let $x$ and $y$ be elements of $G$. Prove that $xy=yx$ if and only if $y^{-1}xy=x$ if and only if $x^{-1}y^{-1}xy=1$.

name: exercise_1_1_20
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Group G] {x : G} :
  orderOf x = orderOf x⁻¹ :=
natural_language_statement: For $x$ an element in $G$ show that $x$ and $x^{-1}$ have the same order.

name: exercise_1_1_22a
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Group G] (x g : G) :
  orderOf x = orderOf (g⁻¹ * x * g) :=
natural_language_statement: If $x$ and $g$ are elements of the group $G$, prove that $|x|=\left|g^{-1} x g\right|$.

name: exercise_1_1_22b
formal_statement:
{G: Type*} [Group G] (a b : G) :
  orderOf (a * b) = orderOf (b * a) :=
natural_language_statement: Deduce that $|a b|=|b a|$ for all $a, b \in G$.

name: exercise_1_1_25
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Group G]
  (h : ∀ x : G, x ^ 2 = 1) : ∀ a b : G, a*b = b*a :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that if $x^{2}=1$ for all $x \in G$ then $G$ is abelian.

name: exercise_1_1_29
formal_statement:
{A B : Type*} [Group A] [Group B] :
  ∀ x y : A × B, x*y = y*x ↔ (∀ x y : A, x*y = y*x) ∧
  (∀ x y : B, x*y = y*x) :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that $A \times B$ is an abelian group if and only if both $A$ and $B$ are abelian.

name: exercise_1_1_34
natural_language_statement: If $x$ is an element of infinite order in $G$, prove that the elements $x^{n}, n \in \mathbb{Z}$ are all distinct.

name: exercise_1_3_8
formal_statement: : Infinite (Equiv.Perm ℕ) :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that if $\Omega=\{1,2,3, \ldots\}$ then $S_{\Omega}$ is an infinite group

name: exercise_1_6_4
formal_statement:
:
  IsEmpty (Multiplicative ℝ ≃* Multiplicative ℂ) :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that the multiplicative groups $\mathbb{R}-\{0\}$ and $\mathbb{C}-\{0\}$ are not isomorphic.

name: exercise_1_6_11
formal_statement:
{A B : Type*} [Group A] [Group B] :
  A × B ≃* B × A :=
natural_language_statement: Let $A$ and $B$ be groups. Prove that $A \times B \cong B \times A$.

name: exercise_1_6_17
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Group G] (f : G → G)
  (hf : f = λ g => g⁻¹) :
  ∀ x y : G, f x * f y = f (x*y) ↔ ∀ x y : G, x*y = y*x :=
natural_language_statement: Let $G$ be any group. Prove that the map from $G$ to itself defined by $g \mapsto g^{-1}$ is a homomorphism if and only if $G$ is abelian.

name: exercise_1_6_23
formal_statement:
{G : Type*}
  [Group G] (σ : MulAut G) (hs : ∀ g : G, σ g = 1 → g = 1)
  (hs2 : ∀ g : G, σ (σ g) = g) :
  ∀ x y : G, x*y = y*x :=
natural_language_statement: Let $G$ be a finite group which possesses an automorphism $\sigma$ such that $\sigma(g)=g$ if and only if $g=1$. If $\sigma^{2}$ is the identity map from $G$ to $G$, prove that $G$ is abelian.

name: exercise_2_1_5
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G]
  (hG : card G > 2) (H : Subgroup G) [Fintype H] :
  card H ≠ card G - 1 :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that $G$ cannot have a subgroup $H$ with $|H|=n-1$, where $n=|G|>2$.

name: exercise_2_1_13
natural_language_statement: Let $H$ be a subgroup of the additive group of rational numbers with the property that $1 / x \in H$ for every nonzero element $x$ of $H$. Prove that $H=0$ or $\mathbb{Q}$.

name: exercise_2_4_4
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Group G] (H : Subgroup G) :
  closure ((H : Set G) \ {1}) = ⊤ :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that if $H$ is a subgroup of $G$ then $H$ is generated by the set $H-\{1\}$.

name: exercise_2_4_16a
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Group G] {H : Subgroup G}
  (hH : H ≠ ⊤) :
  ∃ M : Subgroup G, M ≠ ⊤ ∧
  ∀ K : Subgroup G, M ≤ K → K = M ∨ K = ⊤ ∧
  H ≤ M :=
natural_language_statement: A subgroup $M$ of a group $G$ is called a maximal subgroup if $M \neq G$ and the only subgroups of $G$ which contain $M$ are $M$ and $G$. Prove that if $H$ is a proper subgroup of the finite group $G$ then there is a maximal subgroup of $G$ containing $H$.

name: exercise_2_4_16b
natural_language_statement: Show that the subgroup of all rotations in a dihedral group is a maximal subgroup.

name: exercise_2_4_16c
formal_statement:
{n : ℕ} (H : AddSubgroup (ZMod n)) :
  ∃ p : (ZMod n), Prime p ∧ H = AddSubgroup.closure {p} ↔
  (H ≠ ⊤ ∧ ∀ K : AddSubgroup (ZMod n), H ≤ K → K = H ∨ K = ⊤) :=
natural_language_statement: Show that if $G=\langle x\rangle$ is a cyclic group of order $n \geq 1$ then a subgroup $H$ is maximal if and only $H=\left\langle x^{p}\right\rangle$ for some prime $p$ dividing $n$.

name: exercise_3_1_3a
formal_statement:
{A : Type*} [CommGroup A] (B : Subgroup A) :
  ∀ a b : A ⧸ B, a*b = b*a :=
natural_language_statement: Let $A$ be an abelian group and let $B$ be a subgroup of $A$. Prove that $A / B$ is abelian.

name: exercise_3_1_22a
formal_statement:
(G : Type*) [Group G] (H K : Subgroup G)
  [Normal H] [Normal K] :
  Normal (H ⊓ K) :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that if $H$ and $K$ are normal subgroups of a group $G$ then their intersection $H \cap K$ is also a normal subgroup of $G$.

name: exercise_3_1_22b
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Group G] (I : Type*)
  (H : I → Subgroup G) (hH : ∀ i : I, Normal (H i)) :
  Normal (⨅ (i : I), H i):=
natural_language_statement: Prove that the intersection of an arbitrary nonempty collection of normal subgroups of a group is a normal subgroup (do not assume the collection is countable).

name: exercise_3_2_8
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Group G] (H K : Subgroup G)
  [Fintype H] [Fintype K]
  (hHK : Nat.Coprime (card H) (card K)) :
  H ⊓ K = ⊥ :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that if $H$ and $K$ are finite subgroups of $G$ whose orders are relatively prime then $H \cap K=1$.

name: exercise_3_2_11
natural_language_statement: Let $H \leq K \leq G$. Prove that $|G: H|=|G: K| \cdot|K: H|$ (do not assume $G$ is finite).

name: exercise_3_2_16
formal_statement:
(p : ℕ) (hp : Nat.Prime p) (a : ℕ) :
  Nat.Coprime a p → a ^ p ≡ a [ZMOD p] :=
natural_language_statement: Use Lagrange's Theorem in the multiplicative group $(\mathbb{Z} / p \mathbb{Z})^{\times}$to prove Fermat's Little Theorem: if $p$ is a prime then $a^{p} \equiv a(\bmod p)$ for all $a \in \mathbb{Z}$.

name: exercise_3_2_21a
formal_statement: (H : AddSubgroup ℚ) (hH : H ≠ ⊤) : H.index = 0 :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that $\mathbb{Q}$ has no proper subgroups of finite index.

name: exercise_3_3_3
formal_statement:
{p : Nat.Primes} {G : Type*} [Group G]
  {H : Subgroup G} [hH : H.Normal] (hH1 : H.index = p) :
  ∀ K : Subgroup G, K ≤ H ∨ H ⊔ K = ⊤ ∨ (K ⊓ H).relindex K = p :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that if $H$ is a normal subgroup of $G$ of prime index $p$ then for all $K \leq G$ either $K \leq H$, or $G=H K$ and $|K: K \cap H|=p$.

name: exercise_3_4_1
formal_statement:
(G : Type*) [CommGroup G] [IsSimpleGroup G] :
    IsCyclic G ∧ ∃ G_fin : Fintype G, Nat.Prime (@card G G_fin) :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that if $G$ is an abelian simple group then $G \cong Z_{p}$ for some prime $p$ (do not assume $G$ is a finite group).

name: exercise_3_4_4
natural_language_statement: Use Cauchy's Theorem and induction to show that a finite abelian group has a subgroup of order $n$ for each positive divisor $n$ of its order.

name: exercise_3_4_5a
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Group G]
  (H : Subgroup G) [IsSolvable G] : IsSolvable H :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that subgroups of a solvable group are solvable.

name: exercise_3_4_5b
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Group G] [IsSolvable G]
  (H : Subgroup G) [Normal H] :
  IsSolvable (G ⧸ H) :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that quotient groups of a solvable group are solvable.

name: exercise_3_4_11
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Group G] [IsSolvable G]
  {H : Subgroup G} (hH : H ≠ ⊥) [H.Normal] :
  ∃ A ≤ H, A.Normal ∧ ∀ a b : A, a*b = b*a :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that if $H$ is a nontrivial normal subgroup of the solvable group $G$ then there is a nontrivial subgroup $A$ of $H$ with $A \unlhd G$ and $A$ abelian.

name: exercise_4_2_8
natural_language_statement: Prove that if $H$ has finite index $n$ then there is a normal subgroup $K$ of $G$ with $K \leq H$ and $|G: K| \leq n!$.

name: exercise_4_3_26
formal_statement:
{α : Type*} [Fintype α] (ha : card α > 1)
  (h_tran : ∀ a b: α, ∃ σ : Equiv.Perm α, σ a = b) :
  ∃ σ : Equiv.Perm α, ∀ a : α, σ a ≠ a :=
natural_language_statement: Let $G$ be a transitive permutation group on the finite set $A$ with $|A|>1$. Show that there is some $\sigma \in G$ such that $\sigma(a) \neq a$ for all $a \in A$.

name: exercise_4_2_9a
natural_language_statement: Prove that if $p$ is a prime and $G$ is a group of order $p^{\alpha}$ for some $\alpha \in \mathbb{Z}^{+}$, then every subgroup of index $p$ is normal in $G$.

name: exercise_4_2_14
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Fintype G] [Group G]
  (hG : ¬ (card G).Prime) (hG1 : ∀ k : ℕ, k ∣ card G →
  ∃ (H : Subgroup G) (fH : Fintype H), @card H fH = k) :
  ¬ IsSimpleGroup G :=
natural_language_statement: Let $G$ be a finite group of composite order $n$ with the property that $G$ has a subgroup of order $k$ for each positive integer $k$ dividing $n$. Prove that $G$ is not simple.

name: exercise_4_4_2
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Fintype G] [Group G]
  {p q : Nat.Primes} (hpq : p ≠ q) (hG : card G = p*q) :
  IsCyclic G :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that if $G$ is an abelian group of order $p q$, where $p$ and $q$ are distinct primes, then $G$ is cyclic.

name: exercise_4_4_6a
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Group G] (H : Subgroup G)
  [Characteristic H] : Normal H  :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that characteristic subgroups are normal.

name: exercise_4_4_6b
formal_statement:
:
  ∃ (G : Type*) (hG : Group G) (H : @Subgroup G hG), @Characteristic G hG H  ∧ ¬ @Normal G hG H :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that there exists a normal subgroup that is not characteristic.

name: exercise_4_4_7
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Group G] {H : Subgroup G} [Fintype H]
  (hH : ∀ (K : Subgroup G) (fK : Fintype K), card H = @card K fK → H = K) :
  H.Characteristic :=
natural_language_statement: If $H$ is the unique subgroup of a given order in a group $G$ prove $H$ is characteristic in $G$.

name: exercise_4_4_8a
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Group G] (H K : Subgroup G)
  (hHK : H ≤ K) [hHK1 : (H.subgroupOf K).Normal] [hK : K.Normal] :
  H.Normal :=
natural_language_statement: Let $G$ be a group with subgroups $H$ and $K$ with $H \leq K$. Prove that if $H$ is characteristic in $K$ and $K$ is normal in $G$ then $H$ is normal in $G$.

name: exercise_4_5_1a
formal_statement:
{p : ℕ} {G : Type*} [Group G]
  {P : Subgroup G} (hP : IsPGroup p P) (H : Subgroup G)
  (hH : P ≤ H) : IsPGroup p H :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that if $P \in \operatorname{Syl}_{p}(G)$ and $H$ is a subgroup of $G$ containing $P$ then $P \in \operatorname{Syl}_{p}(H)$.

name: exercise_4_5_13
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G]
  (hG : card G = 56) :
  ∃ (p : ℕ) (P : Sylow p G), P.Normal :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that a group of order 56 has a normal Sylow $p$-subgroup for some prime $p$ dividing its order.

name: exercise_4_5_14
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G]
  (hG : card G = 312) :
  ∃ (p : ℕ) (P : Sylow p G), P.Normal :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that a group of order 312 has a normal Sylow $p$-subgroup for some prime $p$ dividing its order.

name: exercise_4_5_15
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G]
  (hG : card G = 351) :
  ∃ (p : ℕ) (P : Sylow p G), P.Normal :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that a group of order 351 has a normal Sylow $p$-subgroup for some prime $p$ dividing its order.

name: exercise_4_5_16
formal_statement:
{p q r : ℕ} {G : Type*} [Group G]
  [Fintype G]  (hpqr : p < q ∧ q < r)
  (hpqr1 : p.Prime ∧ q.Prime ∧ r.Prime)(hG : card G = p*q*r) :
  Nonempty (Sylow p G) ∨ Nonempty (Sylow q G) ∨ Nonempty (Sylow r G) :=
natural_language_statement: Let $|G|=p q r$, where $p, q$ and $r$ are primes with $p<q<r$. Prove that $G$ has a normal Sylow subgroup for either $p, q$ or $r$.

name: exercise_4_5_17
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Fintype G] [Group G]
  (hG : card G = 105) :
  Nonempty (Sylow 5 G) ∧ Nonempty (Sylow 7 G) :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that if $|G|=105$ then $G$ has a normal Sylow 5 -subgroup and a normal Sylow 7-subgroup.

name: exercise_4_5_18
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Fintype G] [Group G]
  (hG : card G = 200) :
  ∃ N : Sylow 5 G, N.Normal :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that a group of order 200 has a normal Sylow 5-subgroup.

name: exercise_4_5_19
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Fintype G] [Group G]
  (hG : card G = 6545) : ¬ IsSimpleGroup G :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that if $|G|=6545$ then $G$ is not simple.

name: exercise_4_5_20
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Fintype G] [Group G]
  (hG : card G = 1365) : ¬ IsSimpleGroup G :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that if $|G|=1365$ then $G$ is not simple.

name: exercise_4_5_21
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Fintype G] [Group G]
  (hG : card G = 2907) : ¬ IsSimpleGroup G :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that if $|G|=2907$ then $G$ is not simple.

name: exercise_4_5_22
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Fintype G] [Group G]
  (hG : card G = 132) : ¬ IsSimpleGroup G :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that if $|G|=132$ then $G$ is not simple.

name: exercise_4_5_23
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Fintype G] [Group G]
  (hG : card G = 462) : ¬ IsSimpleGroup G :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that if $|G|=462$ then $G$ is not simple.

name: exercise_4_5_28
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G]
  (hG : card G = 105) (P : Sylow 3 G) [hP : P.Normal] :
  CommGroup G :=
natural_language_statement: Let $G$ be a group of order 105. Prove that if a Sylow 3-subgroup of $G$ is normal then $G$ is abelian.

name: exercise_4_5_33
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G] {p : ℕ}
  (P : Sylow p G) [hP : P.Normal] (H : Subgroup G) [Fintype H] :
  ∀ R : Sylow p H, R.toSubgroup = (H ⊓ P.toSubgroup).subgroupOf H ∧
  Nonempty (Sylow p H) :=
natural_language_statement: Let $P$ be a normal Sylow $p$-subgroup of $G$ and let $H$ be any subgroup of $G$. Prove that $P \cap H$ is the unique Sylow $p$-subgroup of $H$.

name: exercise_5_4_2
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Group G] (H : Subgroup G) :
  H.Normal ↔ ⁅(⊤ : Subgroup G), H⁆ ≤ H :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that a subgroup $H$ of $G$ is normal if and only if $[G, H] \leq H$.

name: exercise_7_1_2
formal_statement:
{R : Type*} [Ring R] {u : R}
  (hu : IsUnit u) : IsUnit (-u) :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that if $u$ is a unit in $R$ then so is $-u$.

name: exercise_7_1_11
formal_statement:
{R : Type*} [Ring R] [IsDomain R]
  {x : R} (hx : x^2 = 1) : x = 1 ∨ x = -1 :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that if $R$ is an integral domain and $x^{2}=1$ for some $x \in R$ then $x=\pm 1$.

name: exercise_7_1_12
formal_statement:
{F : Type*} [Field F] {K : Subring F}
  (hK : (1 : F) ∈ K) : IsDomain K :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that any subring of a field which contains the identity is an integral domain.

name: exercise_7_1_15
formal_statement:
{R : Type*} [Ring R] (hR : ∀ a : R, a^2 = a) :
  CommRing R :=
natural_language_statement: A ring $R$ is called a Boolean ring if $a^{2}=a$ for all $a \in R$. Prove that every Boolean ring is commutative.

name: exercise_7_2_2
formal_statement:
{R : Type*} [Ring R] (p : Polynomial R) :
  p ∣ 0 ↔ ∃ b : R, b ≠ 0 ∧ b • p = 0 :=
natural_language_statement: Let $p(x)=a_{n} x^{n}+a_{n-1} x^{n-1}+\cdots+a_{1} x+a_{0}$ be an element of the polynomial ring $R[x]$. Prove that $p(x)$ is a zero divisor in $R[x]$ if and only if there is a nonzero $b \in R$ such that $b p(x)=0$.

name: exercise_7_2_12
formal_statement:
{R G : Type*} [Ring R] [Group G] [Fintype G] :
  ∑ g : G, MonoidAlgebra.of R G g ∈ center (MonoidAlgebra R G) :=
natural_language_statement: Let $G=\left\{g_{1}, \ldots, g_{n}\right\}$ be a finite group. Prove that the element $N=g_{1}+g_{2}+\ldots+g_{n}$ is in the center of the group ring $R G$.

name: exercise_7_3_16
formal_statement:
{R S : Type*} [Ring R] [Ring S]
  {φ : R →+* S} (hf : Function.Surjective φ) :
  φ '' (center R) ⊂ center S :=
natural_language_statement: Let $\varphi: R \rightarrow S$ be a surjective homomorphism of rings. Prove that the image of the center of $R$ is contained in the center of $S$.

name: exercise_7_3_37
formal_statement:
{p m : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) :
  IsNilpotent (span ({↑p} : Set $ ZMod $ p^m) : Ideal $ ZMod $ p^m) :=
natural_language_statement: An ideal $N$ is called nilpotent if $N^{n}$ is the zero ideal for some $n \geq 1$. Prove that the ideal $p \mathbb{Z} / p^{m} \mathbb{Z}$ is a nilpotent ideal in the ring $\mathbb{Z} / p^{m} \mathbb{Z}$.

name: exercise_7_4_27
formal_statement:
{R : Type*} [CommRing R] (hR : (0 : R) ≠ 1)
  {a : R} (ha : IsNilpotent a) (b : R) :
  IsUnit (1-a*b) :=
natural_language_statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with $1 \neq 0$. Prove that if $a$ is a nilpotent element of $R$ then $1-a b$ is a unit for all $b \in R$.

name: exercise_8_1_12
formal_statement:
{N : ℕ} (hN : N > 0) {M M': ℤ} {d : ℕ}
  (hMN : M.gcd N = 1) (hMd : d.gcd N.totient = 1)
  (hM' : M' ≡ M^d [ZMOD N]) :
  ∃ d' : ℕ, d' * d ≡ 1 [ZMOD N.totient] ∧
  M ≡ M'^d' [ZMOD N] :=
natural_language_statement: Let $N$ be a positive integer. Let $M$ be an integer relatively prime to $N$ and let $d$ be an integer relatively prime to $\varphi(N)$, where $\varphi$ denotes Euler's $\varphi$-function. Prove that if $M_{1} \equiv M^{d} \pmod N$ then $M \equiv M_{1}^{d^{\prime}} \pmod N$ where $d^{\prime}$ is the inverse of $d \bmod \varphi(N)$: $d d^{\prime} \equiv 1 \pmod {\varphi(N)}$.

name: exercise_8_2_4
formal_statement:
{R : Type*} [Ring R][NoZeroDivisors R]
  [CancelCommMonoidWithZero R] [GCDMonoid R]
  (h1 : ∀ a b : R, a ≠ 0 → b ≠ 0 → ∃ r s : R, gcd a b = r*a + s*b)
  (h2 : ∀ a : ℕ → R, (∀ i j : ℕ, i < j → a i ∣ a j) →
  ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ N, ∃ u : R, IsUnit u ∧ a n = u * a N) :
  IsPrincipalIdealRing R :=
natural_language_statement: Let $R$ be an integral domain. Prove that if the following two conditions hold then $R$ is a Principal Ideal Domain: (i) any two nonzero elements $a$ and $b$ in $R$ have a greatest common divisor which can be written in the form $r a+s b$ for some $r, s \in R$, and (ii) if $a_{1}, a_{2}, a_{3}, \ldots$ are nonzero elements of $R$ such that $a_{i+1} \mid a_{i}$ for all $i$, then there is a positive integer $N$ such that $a_{n}$ is a unit times $a_{N}$ for all $n \geq N$.

name: exercise_8_3_4
natural_language_statement: Prove that if an integer is the sum of two rational squares, then it is the sum of two integer squares.

name: exercise_8_3_5a
formal_statement:
{n : ℤ} (hn0 : n > 3) (hn1 : Squarefree n) :
  Irreducible (2 : Zsqrtd $ -n) ∧
  Irreducible (⟨0, 1⟩ : Zsqrtd $ -n) ∧
  Irreducible (1 + ⟨0, 1⟩ : Zsqrtd $ -n) :=
natural_language_statement: Let $R=\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{-n}]$ where $n$ is a squarefree integer greater than 3. Prove that $2, \sqrt{-n}$ and $1+\sqrt{-n}$ are irreducibles in $R$.

name: exercise_8_3_6a
formal_statement:
{R : Type} [Ring R]
  (hR : R = (GaussianInt ⧸ span ({⟨0, 1⟩} : Set GaussianInt))) :
  IsField R ∧ ∃ finR : Fintype R, @card R finR = 2 :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that the quotient ring $\mathbb{Z}[i] /(1+i)$ is a field of order 2.

name: exercise_8_3_6b
formal_statement:
{q : ℕ} (hq0 : q.Prime)
  (hq1 : q ≡ 3 [ZMOD 4]) {R : Type} [Ring R]
  (hR : R = (GaussianInt ⧸ span ({↑q} : Set GaussianInt))) :
  IsField R ∧ ∃ finR : Fintype R, @card R finR = q^2 :=
natural_language_statement: Let $q \in \mathbb{Z}$ be a prime with $q \equiv 3 \bmod 4$. Prove that the quotient ring $\mathbb{Z}[i] /(q)$ is a field with $q^{2}$ elements.

name: exercise_9_1_6
formal_statement:
: ¬ Submodule.IsPrincipal
  (span ({MvPolynomial.X 0, MvPolynomial.X 1} : Set (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) ℚ))) :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that $(x, y)$ is not a principal ideal in $\mathbb{Q}[x, y]$.

name: exercise_9_1_10
natural_language_statement: Prove that the ring $\mathbb{Z}\left[x_{1}, x_{2}, x_{3}, \ldots\right] /\left(x_{1} x_{2}, x_{3} x_{4}, x_{5} x_{6}, \ldots\right)$ contains infinitely many minimal prime ideals.

name: exercise_9_3_2
formal_statement:
{f g : Polynomial ℚ} (i j : ℕ)
  (hfg : ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ a : ℤ, (f*g).coeff = a) :
  ∃ a : ℤ, f.coeff i * g.coeff j = a :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that if $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ are polynomials with rational coefficients whose product $f(x) g(x)$ has integer coefficients, then the product of any coefficient of $g(x)$ with any coefficient of $f(x)$ is an integer.

name: exercise_9_4_2a
formal_statement: : Irreducible (X^4 - 4*X^3 + 6 : Polynomial ℤ) :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that $x^4-4x^3+6$ is irreducible in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$.

name: exercise_9_4_2b
formal_statement:
: Irreducible
  (X^6 + 30*X^5 - 15*X^3 + 6*X - 120 : Polynomial ℤ) :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that $x^6+30x^5-15x^3 + 6x-120$ is irreducible in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$.

name: exercise_9_4_2c
formal_statement:
: Irreducible
  (X^4 + 4*X^3 + 6*X^2 + 2*X + 1 : Polynomial ℤ) :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that $x^4+4x^3+6x^2+2x+1$ is irreducible in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$.

name: exercise_9_4_2d
formal_statement:
{p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime ∧ p > 2)
  {f : Polynomial ℤ} (hf : f = (X + 2)^p):
  Irreducible (∑ n in (f.support \ {0}), (f.coeff n : Polynomial ℤ) * X ^ (n-1) :
  Polynomial ℤ) :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that $\frac{(x+2)^p-2^p}{x}$, where $p$ is an odd prime, is irreducible in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$.

name: exercise_9_4_9
formal_statement:
:
  Irreducible (X^2 - C Zsqrtd.sqrtd : Polynomial (Zsqrtd 2)) :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that the polynomial $x^{2}-\sqrt{2}$ is irreducible over $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{2}]$. You may assume that $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{2}]$ is a U.F.D.

name: exercise_9_4_11
formal_statement:
:
  Irreducible ((MvPolynomial.X 0)^2 + (MvPolynomial.X 1)^2 - 1 : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) ℚ) :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that $x^2+y^2-1$ is irreducible in $\mathbb{Q}[x,y]$.

name: exercise_11_1_13
formal_statement:
{ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] :
  (ι → ℝ) ≃ₗ[ℚ] ℝ :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that as vector spaces over $\mathbb{Q}, \mathbb{R}^n \cong \mathbb{R}$, for all $n \in \mathbb{Z}^{+}$.

name: exercise_2_1_18
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Group G]
  [Fintype G] (hG2 : Even (card G)) :
  ∃ (a : G), a ≠ 1 ∧ a = a⁻¹ :=
natural_language_statement: If $G$ is a finite group of even order, show that there must be an element $a \neq e$ such that $a=a^{-1}$.

name: exercise_2_1_21
formal_statement:
(G : Type*) [Group G] [Fintype G]
  (hG : card G = 5) :
  CommGroup G :=
natural_language_statement: Show that a group of order 5 must be abelian.

name: exercise_2_1_26
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Group G]
  [Fintype G] (a : G) : ∃ (n : ℕ), a ^ n = 1 :=
natural_language_statement: If $G$ is a finite group, prove that, given $a \in G$, there is a positive integer $n$, depending on $a$, such that $a^n = e$.

name: exercise_2_1_27
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Group G]
  [Fintype G] : ∃ (m : ℕ), ∀ (a : G), a ^ m = 1 :=
natural_language_statement: If $G$ is a finite group, prove that there is an integer $m > 0$ such that $a^m = e$ for all $a \in G$.

name: exercise_2_2_3
natural_language_statement: If $G$ is a group in which $(a b)^{i}=a^{i} b^{i}$ for three consecutive integers $i$, prove that $G$ is abelian.

name: exercise_2_2_5
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Group G]
  (h : ∀ (a b : G), (a * b) ^ 3 = a ^ 3 * b ^ 3 ∧ (a * b) ^ 5 = a ^ 5 * b ^ 5) :
  CommGroup G :=
natural_language_statement: Let $G$ be a group in which $(a b)^{3}=a^{3} b^{3}$ and $(a b)^{5}=a^{5} b^{5}$ for all $a, b \in G$. Show that $G$ is abelian.

name: exercise_2_2_6c
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Group G] {n : ℕ} (hn : n > 1)
  (h : ∀ (a b : G), (a * b) ^ n = a ^ n * b ^ n) :
  ∀ (a b : G), (a * b * a⁻¹ * b⁻¹) ^ (n * (n - 1)) = 1 :=
natural_language_statement: Let $G$ be a group in which $(a b)^{n}=a^{n} b^{n}$ for some fixed integer $n>1$ for all $a, b \in G$. For all $a, b \in G$, prove that $\left(a b a^{-1} b^{-1}\right)^{n(n-1)}=e$.

name: exercise_2_3_17
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Mul G] [Group G] (a x : G) :
  centralizer {x⁻¹*a*x} =
  (λ g : G => x⁻¹*g*x) '' (centralizer {a}) :=
natural_language_statement: If $G$ is a group and $a, x \in G$, prove that $C\left(x^{-1} a x\right)=x^{-1} C(a) x$

name: exercise_2_3_16
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Group G]
  (hG : ∀ H : Subgroup G, H = ⊤ ∨ H = ⊥) :
  IsCyclic G ∧ ∃ (p : ℕ) (Fin : Fintype G), Nat.Prime p ∧ @card G Fin = p :=
natural_language_statement: If a group $G$ has no proper subgroups, prove that $G$ is cyclic of order $p$, where $p$ is a prime number.

name: exercise_2_4_36
formal_statement:
{a n : ℕ} (h : a > 1) :
  n ∣ (a ^ n - 1).totient :=
natural_language_statement: If $a > 1$ is an integer, show that $n \mid \varphi(a^n - 1)$, where $\phi$ is the Euler $\varphi$-function.

name: exercise_2_5_23
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Group G]
  (hG : ∀ (H : Subgroup G), H.Normal) (a b : G) :
  ∃ (j : ℤ) , b*a = a^j * b:=
natural_language_statement: Let $G$ be a group such that all subgroups of $G$ are normal in $G$. If $a, b \in G$, prove that $ba = a^jb$ for some $j$.

name: exercise_2_5_30
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G]
  {p m : ℕ} (hp : Nat.Prime p) (hp1 : ¬ p ∣ m) (hG : card G = p*m)
  {H : Subgroup G} [Fintype H] [H.Normal] (hH : card H = p):
  Subgroup.Characteristic H :=
natural_language_statement: Suppose that $|G| = pm$, where $p \nmid m$ and $p$ is a prime. If $H$ is a normal subgroup of order $p$ in $G$, prove that $H$ is characteristic.

name: exercise_2_5_31
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [CommGroup G] [Fintype G]
  {p m n : ℕ} (hp : Nat.Prime p) (hp1 : ¬ p ∣ m) (hG : card G = p^n*m)
  {H : Subgroup G} [Fintype H] (hH : card H = p^n) :
  Subgroup.Characteristic H :=
natural_language_statement: Suppose that $G$ is an abelian group of order $p^nm$ where $p \nmid m$ is a prime. If $H$ is a subgroup of $G$ of order $p^n$, prove that $H$ is a characteristic subgroup of $G$.

name: exercise_2_5_37
formal_statement:
(G : Type*) [Group G] [Fintype G]
  (hG : card G = 6) (hG' : IsEmpty (CommGroup G)) :
  G ≃* Equiv.Perm (Fin 3) :=
natural_language_statement: If $G$ is a nonabelian group of order 6, prove that $G \simeq S_3$.

name: exercise_2_5_43
formal_statement:
(G : Type*) [Group G] [Fintype G]
  (hG : card G = 9) :
  CommGroup G :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that a group of order 9 must be abelian.

name: exercise_2_5_44
natural_language_statement: Prove that a group of order $p^2$, $p$ a prime, has a normal subgroup of order $p$.

name: exercise_2_5_52
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G]
  (φ : G ≃* G) {I : Finset G} (hI : ∀ x ∈ I, φ x = x⁻¹)
  (hI1 : (0.75 : ℚ) * card G ≤ card I) :
  ∀ x : G, φ x = x⁻¹ ∧ ∀ x y : G, x*y = y*x :=
natural_language_statement: Let $G$ be a finite group and $\varphi$ an automorphism of $G$ such that $\varphi(x) = x^{-1}$ for more than three-fourths of the elements of $G$. Prove that $\varphi(y) = y^{-1}$ for all $y \in G$, and so $G$ is abelian.

name: exercise_2_6_15
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [CommGroup G] {m n : ℕ}
  (hm : ∃ (g : G), orderOf g = m)
  (hn : ∃ (g : G), orderOf g = n)
  (hmn : m.Coprime n) :
  ∃ (g : G), orderOf g = m * n :=
natural_language_statement: If $G$ is an abelian group and if $G$ has an element of order $m$ and one of order $n$, where $m$ and $n$ are relatively prime, prove that $G$ has an element of order $mn$.

name: exercise_2_7_7
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Group G] {G' : Type*} [Group G']
  (φ : G →* G') (N : Subgroup G) [N.Normal] :
  (Subgroup.map φ N).Normal  :=
natural_language_statement: If $\varphi$ is a homomorphism of $G$ onto $G'$ and $N \triangleleft G$, show that $\varphi(N) \triangleleft G'$.

name: exercise_2_8_12
formal_statement:
{G H : Type*} [Fintype G] [Fintype H]
  [Group G] [Group H] (hG : card G = 21) (hH : card H = 21)
  (hG1 : IsEmpty (CommGroup G)) (hH1 : IsEmpty (CommGroup H)) :
  G ≃* H :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that any two nonabelian groups of order 21 are isomorphic.

name: exercise_2_8_15
formal_statement:
{G H: Type*} [Fintype G] [Group G] [Fintype H]
  [Group H] {p q : ℕ} (hp : Nat.Prime p) (hq : Nat.Prime q)
  (h : p > q) (h1 : q ∣ p - 1) (hG : card G = p*q) (hH : card G = p*q) :
  G ≃* H :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that if $p > q$ are two primes such that $q \mid p - 1$, then any two nonabelian groups of order $pq$ are isomorphic.

name: exercise_2_9_2
formal_statement:
{G H : Type*} [Fintype G] [Fintype H] [Group G]
  [Group H] (hG : IsCyclic G) (hH : IsCyclic H) :
  IsCyclic (G × H) ↔ (card G).Coprime (card H) :=
natural_language_statement: If $G_1$ and $G_2$ are cyclic groups of orders $m$ and $n$, respectively, prove that $G_1 \times G_2$ is cyclic if and only if $m$ and $n$ are relatively prime.

name: exercise_2_10_1
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Group G] (A : Subgroup G)
  [A.Normal] {b : G} (hp : Nat.Prime (orderOf b)) :
  A ⊓ (Subgroup.closure {b}) = ⊥ :=
natural_language_statement: Let $A$ be a normal subgroup of a group $G$, and suppose that $b \in G$ is an element of prime order $p$, and that $b \not\in A$. Show that $A \cap (b) = (e)$.

name: exercise_2_11_6
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Group G] {p : ℕ} (hp : Nat.Prime p)
  {P : Sylow p G} (hP : P.Normal) :
  ∀ (Q : Sylow p G), P = Q :=
natural_language_statement: If $P$ is a $p$-Sylow subgroup of $G$ and $P \triangleleft G$, prove that $P$ is the only $p$-Sylow subgroup of $G$.

name: exercise_2_11_7
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [Group G] {p : ℕ} (hp : Nat.Prime p)
  {P : Sylow p G} (hP : P.Normal) :
  Subgroup.Characteristic (P : Subgroup G) :=
natural_language_statement: If $P \triangleleft G$, $P$ a $p$-Sylow subgroup of $G$, prove that $\varphi(P) = P$ for every automorphism $\varphi$ of $G$.

name: exercise_2_11_22
formal_statement:
{p : ℕ} {n : ℕ} {G : Type*} [Fintype G]
  [Group G] (hp : Nat.Prime p) (hG : card G = p ^ n) {K : Subgroup G}
  [Fintype K] (hK : card K = p ^ (n-1)) :
  K.Normal :=
natural_language_statement: Show that any subgroup of order $p^{n-1}$ in a group $G$ of order $p^n$ is normal in $G$.

name: exercise_3_2_21
natural_language_statement: If $\sigma, \tau$ are two permutations that disturb no common element and $\sigma \tau = e$, prove that $\sigma = \tau = e$.

name: exercise_4_1_19
formal_statement: : Infinite {x : Quaternion ℝ | x^2 = -1} :=
natural_language_statement: Show that there is an infinite number of solutions to $x^2 = -1$ in the quaternions.

name: exercise_4_1_34
formal_statement: : Equiv.Perm (Fin 3) ≃* Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (Fin 2) (ZMod 2) :=
natural_language_statement: Let $T$ be the group of $2\times 2$ matrices $A$ with entries in the field $\mathbb{Z}_2$ such that $\det A$ is not equal to 0. Prove that $T$ is isomorphic to $S_3$, the symmetric group of degree 3.

name: exercise_4_2_5
formal_statement:
{R : Type*} [Ring R]
  (h : ∀ x : R, x ^ 3 = x) : CommRing R :=
natural_language_statement: Let $R$ be a ring in which $x^3 = x$ for every $x \in R$. Prove that $R$ is commutative.

name: exercise_4_2_6
formal_statement:
{R : Type*} [Ring R] (a x : R)
  (h : a ^ 2 = 0) : a * (a * x + x * a) = (x + x * a) * a :=
natural_language_statement: If $a^2 = 0$ in $R$, show that $ax + xa$ commutes with $a$.

name: exercise_4_2_9
formal_statement:
{p : ℕ} (hp : Nat.Prime p) (hp1 : Odd p) :
  ∃ (a b : ℤ), (a / b : ℚ) = ∑ i in Finset.range p, 1 / (i + 1) → ↑p ∣ a :=
natural_language_statement: Let $p$ be an odd prime and let $1 + \frac{1}{2} + ... + \frac{1}{p - 1} = \frac{a}{b}$, where $a, b$ are integers. Show that $p \mid a$.

name: exercise_4_3_1
formal_statement:
{R : Type*} [CommRing R] (a : R) :
  ∃ I : Ideal R, {x : R | x*a=0} = I :=
natural_language_statement: If $R$ is a commutative ring and $a \in R$, let $L(a) = \{x \in R \mid xa = 0\}$. Prove that $L(a)$ is an ideal of $R$.

name: exercise_4_3_25
formal_statement:
(I : Ideal (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℝ)) :
  I = ⊥ ∨ I = ⊤ :=
natural_language_statement: Let $R$ be the ring of $2 \times 2$ matrices over the real numbers; suppose that $I$ is an ideal of $R$. Show that $I = (0)$ or $I = R$.

name: exercise_4_4_9
formal_statement:
(p : ℕ) (hp : Nat.Prime p) :
  (∃ S : Finset (ZMod p), S.card = (p-1)/2 ∧ ∃ x : ZMod p, x^2 = p) ∧
  (∃ S : Finset (ZMod p), S.card = (p-1)/2 ∧ ¬ ∃ x : ZMod p, x^2 = p) :=
natural_language_statement: Show that $(p - 1)/2$ of the numbers $1, 2, \ldots, p - 1$ are quadratic residues and $(p - 1)/2$ are quadratic nonresidues $\mod p$.

name: exercise_4_5_16
formal_statement:
{p n: ℕ} (hp : Nat.Prime p)
  {q : Polynomial (ZMod p)} (hq : Irreducible q) (hn : q.degree = n) :
  ∃ is_fin : Fintype $ Polynomial (ZMod p) ⧸ span ({q} : Set (Polynomial $ ZMod p)),
  @card (Polynomial (ZMod p) ⧸ span {q}) is_fin = p ^ n ∧
  IsField (Polynomial $ ZMod p):=
natural_language_statement: Let $F = \mathbb{Z}_p$ be the field of integers $\mod p$, where $p$ is a prime, and let $q(x) \in F[x]$ be irreducible of degree $n$. Show that $F[x]/(q(x))$ is a field having at exactly $p^n$ elements.

name: exercise_4_5_23
formal_statement:
{p q: Polynomial (ZMod 7)}
  (hp : p = X^3 - 2) (hq : q = X^3 + 2) :
  Irreducible p ∧ Irreducible q ∧
  (Nonempty $ Polynomial (ZMod 7) ⧸ span ({p} : Set $ Polynomial $ ZMod 7) ≃+*
  Polynomial (ZMod 7) ⧸ span ({q} : Set $ Polynomial $ ZMod 7)) :=
natural_language_statement: Let $F = \mathbb{Z}_7$ and let $p(x) = x^3 - 2$ and $q(x) = x^3 + 2$ be in $F[x]$. Show that $p(x)$ and $q(x)$ are irreducible in $F[x]$ and that the fields $F[x]/(p(x))$ and $F[x]/(q(x))$ are isomorphic.

name: exercise_4_5_25
formal_statement:
{p : ℕ} (hp : Nat.Prime p) :
  Irreducible (∑ i : Finset.range p, X ^ p : Polynomial ℚ) :=
natural_language_statement: If $p$ is a prime, show that $q(x) = 1 + x + x^2 + \cdots x^{p - 1}$ is irreducible in $Q[x]$.

name: exercise_4_6_2
formal_statement: : Irreducible (X^3 + 3*X + 2 : Polynomial ℚ) :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that $f(x) = x^3 + 3x + 2$ is irreducible in $Q[x]$.

name: exercise_4_6_3
formal_statement:
:
  Infinite {a : ℤ | Irreducible (X^7 + 15*X^2 - 30*X + (a : Polynomial ℚ) : Polynomial ℚ)} :=
natural_language_statement: Show that there is an infinite number of integers a such that $f(x) = x^7 + 15x^2 - 30x + a$ is irreducible in $Q[x]$.

name: exercise_5_1_8
formal_statement:
{p m n: ℕ} {F : Type*} [Field F]
  (hp : Nat.Prime p) (hF : CharP F p) (a b : F) (hm : m = p ^ n) :
  (a + b) ^ m = a^m + b^m :=
natural_language_statement: If $F$ is a field of characteristic $p \neq 0$, show that $(a + b)^m = a^m + b^m$, where $m = p^n$, for all $a, b \in F$ and any positive integer $n$.

name: exercise_5_2_20
formal_statement:
{F V ι: Type*} [Infinite F] [Field F]
  [AddCommGroup V] [Module F V] {u : ι → Submodule F V}
  (hu : ∀ i : ι, u i ≠ ⊤) :
  (⋃ i : ι, (u i : Set V)) ≠ ⊤ :=
natural_language_statement: Let $V$ be a vector space over an infinite field $F$. Show that $V$ cannot be the set-theoretic union of a finite number of proper subspaces of $V$.

name: exercise_5_3_7
formal_statement:
{K : Type*} [Field K] {F : Subfield K}
  {a : K} (ha : IsAlgebraic F (a ^ 2)) : IsAlgebraic F a :=
natural_language_statement: If $a \in K$ is such that $a^2$ is algebraic over the subfield $F$ of $K$, show that a is algebraic over $F$.

name: exercise_5_3_10
formal_statement: : IsAlgebraic ℚ (cos (Real.pi / 180)) :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that $\cos 1^{\circ}$ is algebraic over $\mathbb{Q}$.

name: exercise_5_4_3
formal_statement:
{a : ℂ} {p : ℂ → ℂ}
  (hp : p = λ (x : ℂ) => x^5 + sqrt 2 * x^3 + sqrt 5 * x^2 + sqrt 7 * x + 11)
  (ha : p a = 0) :
  ∃ p : Polynomial ℂ , p.degree < 80 ∧ a ∈ p.roots ∧
  ∀ n : p.support, ∃ a b : ℤ, p.coeff n = a / b :=
natural_language_statement: If $a \in C$ is such that $p(a) = 0$, where $p(x) = x^5 + \sqrt{2}x^3 + \sqrt{5}x^2 + \sqrt{7}x + \sqrt{11}$, show that $a$ is algebraic over $\mathbb{Q}$ of degree at most 80.

name: exercise_5_5_2
formal_statement: : Irreducible (X^3 - 3*X - 1 : Polynomial ℚ) :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that $x^3 - 3x - 1$ is irreducible over $\mathbb{Q}$.

name: exercise_5_6_14
natural_language_statement: If $F$ is of characteristic $p \neq 0$, show that all the roots of $x^m - x$, where $m = p^n$, are distinct.

name: exercise_1_27
natural_language_statement: For all odd $n$ show that $8 \mid n^{2}-1$.

name: exercise_1_30
natural_language_statement: Prove that $\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{3}+\cdots+\frac{1}{n}$ is not an integer.

name: exercise_1_31
formal_statement: (⟨1, 1⟩ : GaussianInt) ^ 2 ∣ 2 :=
natural_language_statement: Show that 2 is divisible by $(1+i)^{2}$ in $\mathbb{Z}[i]$.

name: exercise_2_4
formal_statement:
{a : ℤ} (ha : a ≠ 0)
  (f_a := λ n m : ℕ => Int.gcd (a^(2^n) + 1) (a^(2^m)+1)) {n m : ℕ}
  (hnm : n > m) :
  (Odd a → f_a n m = 1) ∧ (Even a → f_a n m = 2) :=
natural_language_statement: If $a$ is a nonzero integer, then for $n>m$ show that $\left(a^{2^{n}}+1, a^{2^{m}}+1\right)=1$ or 2 depending on whether $a$ is odd or even.

name: exercise_2_21
formal_statement:
{l : ℕ → ℝ}
  (hl : ∀ p n : ℕ, p.Prime → l (p^n) = log p )
  (hl1 : ∀ m : ℕ, ¬ IsPrimePow m → l m = 0) :
  l = λ n => ∑ d : Nat.divisors n, ArithmeticFunction.moebius (n/d) * log d  :=
natural_language_statement: Define $\wedge(n)=\log p$ if $n$ is a power of $p$ and zero otherwise. Prove that $\sum_{A \mid n} \mu(n / d) \log d$ $=\wedge(n)$.

name: exercise_2_27a
formal_statement: ¬ Summable (λ i : {p : ℤ // Squarefree p} => (1 : ℚ) / i) :=
natural_language_statement: Show that $\sum^{\prime} 1 / n$, the sum being over square free integers, diverges.

name: exercise_3_1
formal_statement: Infinite {p : Nat.Primes // p ≡ -1 [ZMOD 6]} :=
natural_language_statement: Show that there are infinitely many primes congruent to $-1$ modulo 6 .

name: exercise_3_4
natural_language_statement: Show that the equation $3 x^{2}+2=y^{2}$ has no solution in integers.

name: exercise_3_5
natural_language_statement: Show that the equation $7 x^{3}+2=y^{3}$ has no solution in integers.

name: exercise_3_10
formal_statement:
{n : ℕ} (hn0 : ¬ n.Prime) (hn1 : n ≠ 4) :
  Nat.factorial (n-1) ≡ 0 [MOD n] :=
natural_language_statement: If $n$ is not a prime, show that $(n-1) ! \equiv 0(n)$, except when $n=4$.

name: exercise_3_14
formal_statement:
{p q n : ℕ} (hp0 : p.Prime ∧ p > 2)
  (hq0 : q.Prime ∧ q > 2) (hpq0 : p ≠ q) (hpq1 : p - 1 ∣ q - 1)
  (hn : n.gcd (p*q) = 1) :
  n^(q-1) ≡ 1 [MOD p*q] :=
natural_language_statement: Let $p$ and $q$ be distinct odd primes such that $p-1$ divides $q-1$. If $(n, p q)=1$, show that $n^{q-1} \equiv 1(p q)$.

name: exercise_4_4
formal_statement:
{p t: ℕ} (hp0 : p.Prime) (hp1 : p = 4*t + 1)
  (a : ZMod p) :
  IsPrimitiveRoot a p ↔ IsPrimitiveRoot (-a) p :=
natural_language_statement: Consider a prime $p$ of the form $4 t+1$. Show that $a$ is a primitive root modulo $p$ iff $-a$ is a primitive root modulo $p$.

name: exercise_4_5
formal_statement:
{p t : ℕ} (hp0 : p.Prime) (hp1 : p = 4*t + 3)
  (a : ZMod p) :
  IsPrimitiveRoot a p ↔ ((-a) ^ ((p-1)/2) = 1 ∧ ∀ (k : ℕ), k < (p-1)/2 → (-a)^k ≠ 1) :=
natural_language_statement: Consider a prime $p$ of the form $4 t+3$. Show that $a$ is a primitive root modulo $p$ iff $-a$ has order $(p-1) / 2$.

name: exercise_4_6
formal_statement:
{p n : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hpn : p = 2^n + 1) :
  IsPrimitiveRoot 3 p :=
natural_language_statement: If $p=2^{n}+1$ is a Fermat prime, show that 3 is a primitive root modulo $p$.

name: exercise_4_8
formal_statement:
{p a : ℕ} (hp : Odd p) :
  IsPrimitiveRoot a p ↔ (∀ q : ℕ, q ∣ (p-1) → q.Prime → ¬ a^(p-1) ≡ 1 [MOD p]) :=
natural_language_statement: Let $p$ be an odd prime. Show that $a$ is a primitive root modulo $p$ iff $a^{(p-1) / q} \not \equiv 1(p)$ for all prime divisors $q$ of $p-1$.

name: exercise_4_11
formal_statement:
{p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (k s: ℕ)
  (s := ∑ n : Fin p, (n : ℕ) ^ k) :
  ((¬ p - 1 ∣ k) → s ≡ 0 [MOD p]) ∧ (p - 1 ∣ k → s ≡ 0 [MOD p]) :=
natural_language_statement: Prove that $1^{k}+2^{k}+\cdots+(p-1)^{k} \equiv 0(p)$ if $p-1 \nmid k$ and $-1(p)$ if $p-1 \mid k$.

name: exercise_5_13
formal_statement:
{p x: ℤ} (hp : Prime p)
  (hpx : p ∣ (x^4 - x^2 + 1)) : p ≡ 1 [ZMOD 12] :=
natural_language_statement: Show that any prime divisor of $x^{4}-x^{2}+1$ is congruent to 1 modulo 12 .

name: exercise_5_28
formal_statement:
{p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hp1 : p ≡ 1 [MOD 4]):
  ∃ x, x^4 ≡ 2 [MOD p] ↔ ∃ A B, p = A^2 + 64*B^2 :=
natural_language_statement: Show that $x^{4} \equiv 2(p)$ has a solution for $p \equiv 1(4)$ iff $p$ is of the form $A^{2}+64 B^{2}$.

name: exercise_5_37
natural_language_statement: Show that if $a$ is negative then $p \equiv q(4 a) together with p\not | a$ imply $(a / p)=(a / q)$.

name: exercise_12_12
formal_statement: IsAlgebraic ℚ (sin (pi/12)) :=
natural_language_statement: Show that $\sin (\pi / 12)$ is an algebraic number.

name: exercise_18_4
natural_language_statement: Show that 1729 is the smallest positive integer expressible as the sum of two different integral cubes in two ways.

name: exercise_13_1
formal_statement:
(X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] (A : Set X)
  (h1 : ∀ x ∈ A, ∃ U : Set X, x ∈ U ∧ IsOpen U ∧ U ⊆ A) :
  IsOpen A :=
natural_language_statement: Let $X$ be a topological space; let $A$ be a subset of $X$. Suppose that for each $x \in A$ there is an open set $U$ containing $x$ such that $U \subset A$. Show that $A$ is open in $X$.

name: exercise_13_3b
formal_statement:
¬ ∀ X : Type, ∀s : Set (Set X),
  (∀ t : Set X, t ∈ s → (Set.Infinite tᶜ ∨ t = ∅ ∨ t = ⊤)) →
  (Set.Infinite (⋃₀ s)ᶜ ∨ (⋃₀ s) = ∅ ∨ (⋃₀ s) = ⊤) :=
natural_language_statement: Show that the collection $$\mathcal{T}_\infty = \{U | X - U \text{ is infinite or empty or all of X}\}$$ does not need to be a topology on the set $X$.

name: exercise_13_4a1
formal_statement:
(X I : Type*) (T : I → Set (Set X)) (h : ∀ i, is_topology X (T i)) :
  is_topology X (⋂ i : I, T i) :=
natural_language_statement: If $\mathcal{T}_\alpha$ is a family of topologies on $X$, show that $\bigcap \mathcal{T}_\alpha$ is a topology on $X$.

name: exercise_13_4a2
formal_statement:
∃ (X I : Type*) (T : I → Set (Set X)),
  (∀ i, is_topology X (T i)) ∧ ¬  is_topology X (⋂ i : I, T i) :=
natural_language_statement: If $\mathcal{T}_\alpha$ is a family of topologies on $X$, show that $\bigcup \mathcal{T}_\alpha$ does not need to be a topology on $X$.

name: exercise_13_4b1
formal_statement:
(X I : Type*) (T : I → Set (Set X)) (h : ∀ i, is_topology X (T i)) :
  ∃! T', is_topology X T' ∧ (∀ i, T i ⊆ T') ∧
  ∀ T'', is_topology X T'' → (∀ i, T i ⊆ T'') → T'' ⊆ T' :=
natural_language_statement: Let $\mathcal{T}_\alpha$ be a family of topologies on $X$. Show that there is a unique smallest topology on $X$ containing all the collections $\mathcal{T}_\alpha$.

name: exercise_13_4b2
formal_statement:
(X I : Type*) (T : I → Set (Set X)) (h : ∀ i, is_topology X (T i)) :
  ∃! T', is_topology X T' ∧ (∀ i, T' ⊆ T i) ∧
  ∀ T'', is_topology X T'' → (∀ i, T'' ⊆ T i) → T' ⊆ T'' :=
natural_language_statement: Let $\mathcal{T}_\alpha$ be a family of topologies on $X$. Show that there is a unique largest topology on $X$ contained in all the collections $\mathcal{T}_\alpha$.

name: exercise_13_5a
natural_language_statement: Show that if $\mathcal{A}$ is a basis for a topology on $X$, then the topology generated by $\mathcal{A}$ equals the intersection of all topologies on $X$ that contain $\mathcal{A}$.

name: exercise_13_5b
natural_language_statement: Show that if $\mathcal{A}$ is a subbasis for a topology on $X$, then the topology generated by $\mathcal{A}$ equals the intersection of all topologies on $X$ that contain $\mathcal{A}$.

name: exercise_13_6
formal_statement:
:
  ¬ (∀ U, Rl.IsOpen U → K_topology.IsOpen U) ∧ ¬ (∀ U, K_topology.IsOpen U → Rl.IsOpen U) :=
natural_language_statement: Show that the lower limit topology $\mathbb{R}_l$ and $K$-topology $\mathbb{R}_K$ are not comparable.

name: exercise_13_8a
formal_statement:
:
  IsTopologicalBasis {S : Set ℝ | ∃ a b : ℚ, a < b ∧ S = Ioo ↑a ↑b} :=
natural_language_statement: Show that the collection $\{(a,b) \mid a < b, a \text{ and } b \text{ rational}\}$ is a basis that generates the standard topology on $\mathbb{R}$.

name: exercise_13_8b
formal_statement:
(generateFrom {S : Set ℝ | ∃ a b : ℚ, a < b ∧ S = Ico ↑a ↑b}).IsOpen ≠
  (lower_limit_topology ℝ).IsOpen :=
natural_language_statement: Show that the collection $\{(a,b) \mid a < b, a \text{ and } b \text{ rational}\}$ is a basis that generates a topology different from the lower limit topology on $\mathbb{R}$.

name: exercise_16_1
formal_statement:
{X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X]
  (Y : Set X)
  (A : Set Y) :
  ∀ U : Set A, IsOpen U ↔ IsOpen (Subtype.val '' U) :=
natural_language_statement: Show that if $Y$ is a subspace of $X$, and $A$ is a subset of $Y$, then the topology $A$ inherits as a subspace of $Y$ is the same as the topology it inherits as a subspace of $X$.

name: exercise_16_4
formal_statement:
{X Y : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y]
  (π₁ : X × Y → X)
  (π₂ : X × Y → Y)
  (h₁ : π₁ = Prod.fst)
  (h₂ : π₂ = Prod.snd) :
  IsOpenMap π₁ ∧ IsOpenMap π₂ :=
natural_language_statement: A map $f: X \rightarrow Y$ is said to be an open map if for every open set $U$ of $X$, the set $f(U)$ is open in $Y$. Show that $\pi_{1}: X \times Y \rightarrow X$ and $\pi_{2}: X \times Y \rightarrow Y$ are open maps.

name: exercise_16_6
formal_statement:
(S : Set (Set (ℝ × ℝ)))
  (hS : ∀ s, s ∈ S → ∃ a b c d, (rational a ∧ rational b ∧ rational c ∧ rational d
  ∧ s = {x | ∃ x₁ x₂, x = (x₁, x₂) ∧ a < x₁ ∧ x₁ < b ∧ c < x₂ ∧ x₂ < d})) :
  IsTopologicalBasis S :=
natural_language_statement: Show that the countable collection \[\{(a, b) \times (c, d) \mid a < b \text{ and } c < d, \text{ and } a, b, c, d \text{ are rational}\}\] is a basis for $\mathbb{R}^2$.

name: exercise_17_4
formal_statement:
{X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X]
  (U A : Set X) (hU : IsOpen U) (hA : IsClosed A) :
  IsOpen (U \ A) ∧ IsClosed (A \ U) :=
natural_language_statement: Show that if $U$ is open in $X$ and $A$ is closed in $X$, then $U-A$ is open in $X$, and $A-U$ is closed in $X$.

name: exercise_18_8a
formal_statement:
{X Y : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y]
  [LinearOrder Y] [OrderTopology Y] {f g : X → Y}
  (hf : Continuous f) (hg : Continuous g) :
  IsClosed {x | f x ≤ g x} :=
natural_language_statement: Let $Y$ be an ordered set in the order topology. Let $f, g: X \rightarrow Y$ be continuous. Show that the set $\{x \mid f(x) \leq g(x)\}$ is closed in $X$.

name: exercise_18_8b
formal_statement:
{X Y : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y]
  [LinearOrder Y] [OrderTopology Y] {f g : X → Y}
  (hf : Continuous f) (hg : Continuous g) :
  Continuous (λ x => min (f x) (g x)) :=
natural_language_statement: Let $Y$ be an ordered set in the order topology. Let $f, g: X \rightarrow Y$ be continuous. Let $h: X \rightarrow Y$ be the function $h(x)=\min \{f(x), g(x)\}.$ Show that $h$ is continuous.

name: exercise_18_13
formal_statement:
{X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] {Y : Type*} [TopologicalSpace Y]
  [T2Space Y] {A : Set X} {f : A → Y} (hf : Continuous f)
  (g : closure A → Y)
  (g_con : Continuous g) :
  ∀ (g' : closure A → Y), Continuous g' →  (∀ (x : closure A), g x = g' x) :=
natural_language_statement: Let $A \subset X$; let $f: A \rightarrow Y$ be continuous; let $Y$ be Hausdorff. Show that if $f$ may be extended to a continuous function $g: \bar{A} \rightarrow Y$, then $g$ is uniquely determined by $f$.

name: exercise_19_6a
natural_language_statement: Let $\mathbf{x}_1, \mathbf{x}_2, \ldots$ be a sequence of the points of the product space $\prod X_\alpha$. Show that this sequence converges to the point $\mathbf{x}$ if and only if the sequence $\pi_\alpha(\mathbf{x}_i)$ converges to $\pi_\alpha(\mathbf{x})$ for each $\alpha$.

name: exercise_20_2
formal_statement:
[TopologicalSpace (ℝ ×ₗ ℝ)] [OrderTopology (ℝ ×ₗ ℝ)]
  : MetrizableSpace (ℝ ×ₗ ℝ) :=
natural_language_statement: Show that $\mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}$ in the dictionary order topology is metrizable.

name: exercise_21_6a
formal_statement:
(f : ℕ → I → ℝ )
  (h : ∀ x n, f n x = x ^ n) :
  ∀ x, ∃ y, Tendsto (λ n => f n x) atTop (𝓝 y) :=
natural_language_statement: Define $f_{n}:[0,1] \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ by the equation $f_{n}(x)=x^{n}$. Show that the sequence $\left(f_{n}(x)\right)$ converges for each $x \in[0,1]$.

name: exercise_21_6b
formal_statement:
(f : ℕ → I → ℝ )
  (h : ∀ x n, f n x = x ^ n) :
  ¬ ∃ f₀, TendstoUniformly f f₀ atTop :=
natural_language_statement: Define $f_{n}:[0,1] \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ by the equation $f_{n}(x)=x^{n}$. Show that the sequence $\left(f_{n}\right)$ does not converge uniformly.

name: exercise_21_8
formal_statement:
{X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] {Y : Type*} [MetricSpace Y]
  {f : ℕ → X → Y} {x : ℕ → X}
  (hf : ∀ n, Continuous (f n))
  (x₀ : X)
  (hx : Tendsto x atTop (𝓝 x₀))
  (f₀ : X → Y)
  (hh : TendstoUniformly f f₀ atTop) :
  Tendsto (λ n => f n (x n)) atTop (𝓝 (f₀ x₀)) :=
natural_language_statement: Let $X$ be a topological space and let $Y$ be a metric space. Let $f_{n}: X \rightarrow Y$ be a sequence of continuous functions. Let $x_{n}$ be a sequence of points of $X$ converging to $x$. Show that if the sequence $\left(f_{n}\right)$ converges uniformly to $f$, then $\left(f_{n}\left(x_{n}\right)\right)$ converges to $f(x)$.

name: exercise_22_2a
formal_statement:
{X Y : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X]
  [TopologicalSpace Y] (p : X → Y) (h : Continuous p) :
  QuotientMap p ↔ ∃ (f : Y → X), Continuous f ∧ p ∘ f = id :=
natural_language_statement: Let $p: X \rightarrow Y$ be a continuous map. Show that if there is a continuous map $f: Y \rightarrow X$ such that $p \circ f$ equals the identity map of $Y$, then $p$ is a quotient map.

name: exercise_22_2b
formal_statement:
{X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X]
  {A : Set X} (r : X → A) (hr : Continuous r) (h : ∀ x : A, r x = x) :
  QuotientMap r :=
natural_language_statement: If $A \subset X$, a retraction of $X$ onto $A$ is a continuous map $r: X \rightarrow A$ such that $r(a)=a$ for each $a \in A$. Show that a retraction is a quotient map.

name: exercise_22_5
formal_statement:
{X Y : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X]
  [TopologicalSpace Y] (p : X → Y) (hp : IsOpenMap p)
  (A : Set X) (hA : IsOpen A) : IsOpenMap (p ∘ Subtype.val : A → Y) :=
natural_language_statement: Let $p \colon X \rightarrow Y$ be an open map. Show that if $A$ is open in $X$, then the map $q \colon A \rightarrow p(A)$ obtained by restricting $p$ is an open map.

name: exercise_23_2
formal_statement:
{X : Type*}
  [TopologicalSpace X] {A : ℕ → Set X} (hA : ∀ n, IsConnected (A n))
  (hAn : ∀ n, A n ∩ A (n + 1) ≠ ∅) :
  IsConnected (⋃ n, A n) :=
natural_language_statement: Let $\left\{A_{n}\right\}$ be a sequence of connected subspaces of $X$, such that $A_{n} \cap A_{n+1} \neq \varnothing$ for all $n$. Show that $\bigcup A_{n}$ is connected.

name: exercise_23_3
formal_statement:
{X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X]
  [TopologicalSpace X] {A : ℕ → Set X}
  (hAn : ∀ n, IsConnected (A n))
  (A₀ : Set X)
  (hA : IsConnected A₀)
  (h : ∀ n, A₀ ∩ A n ≠ ∅) :
  IsConnected (A₀ ∪ (⋃ n, A n)) :=
natural_language_statement: Let $\left\{A_{\alpha}\right\}$ be a collection of connected subspaces of $X$; let $A$ be a connected subset of $X$. Show that if $A \cap A_{\alpha} \neq \varnothing$ for all $\alpha$, then $A \cup\left(\bigcup A_{\alpha}\right)$ is connected.

name: exercise_23_4
formal_statement:
{X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [CofiniteTopology X]
  (s : Set X) : Infinite s → IsConnected s :=
natural_language_statement: Show that if $X$ is an infinite set, it is connected in the finite complement topology.

name: exercise_23_6
formal_statement:
{X : Type*}
  [TopologicalSpace X] {A C : Set X} (hc : IsConnected C)
  (hCA : C ∩ A ≠ ∅) (hCXA : C ∩ Aᶜ ≠ ∅) :
  C ∩ (frontier A) ≠ ∅ :=
natural_language_statement: Let $A \subset X$. Show that if $C$ is a connected subspace of $X$ that intersects both $A$ and $X-A$, then $C$ intersects $\operatorname{Bd} A$.

name: exercise_23_9
formal_statement:
{X Y : Type*}
  [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y]
  (A₁ A₂ : Set X)
  (B₁ B₂ : Set Y)
  (hA : A₁ ⊂ A₂)
  (hB : B₁ ⊂ B₂)
  (hA : IsConnected A₂)
  (hB : IsConnected B₂) :
  IsConnected ({x | ∃ a b, x = (a, b) ∧ a ∈ A₂ ∧ b ∈ B₂} \
      {x | ∃ a b, x = (a, b) ∧ a ∈ A₁ ∧ b ∈ B₁}) :=
natural_language_statement: Let $A$ be a proper subset of $X$, and let $B$ be a proper subset of $Y$. If $X$ and $Y$ are connected, show that $(X \times Y)-(A \times B)$ is connected.

name: exercise_23_11
formal_statement:
{X Y : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y]
  (p : X → Y) (hq : QuotientMap p)
  (hY : ConnectedSpace Y) (hX : ∀ y : Y, IsConnected (p ⁻¹' {y})) :
  ConnectedSpace X :=
natural_language_statement: Let $p: X \rightarrow Y$ be a quotient map. Show that if each set $p^{-1}(\{y\})$ is connected, and if $Y$ is connected, then $X$ is connected.

name: exercise_24_2
formal_statement:
{f : (Metric.sphere 0 1 : Set ℝ) → ℝ}
  (hf : Continuous f) : ∃ x, f x = f (-x) :=
natural_language_statement: Let $f: S^{1} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ be a continuous map. Show there exists a point $x$ of $S^{1}$ such that $f(x)=f(-x)$.

name: exercise_24_3a
formal_statement:
[TopologicalSpace I] [CompactSpace I]
  (f : I → I) (hf : Continuous f) :
  ∃ (x : I), f x = x :=
natural_language_statement: Let $f \colon X \rightarrow X$ be continuous. Show that if $X = [0, 1]$, there is a point $x$ such that $f(x) = x$. (The point $x$ is called a fixed point of $f$.)

name: exercise_25_4
formal_statement:
{X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X]
  [LocPathConnectedSpace X] (U : Set X) (hU : IsOpen U)
  (hcU : IsConnected U) : IsPathConnected U :=
natural_language_statement: Let $X$ be locally path connected. Show that every connected open set in $X$ is path connected.

name: exercise_25_9
formal_statement:
{G : Type*} [TopologicalSpace G] [Group G]
  [TopologicalGroup G] (C : Set G) (h : C = connectedComponent 1) :
  IsNormalSubgroup C :=
natural_language_statement: Let $G$ be a topological group; let $C$ be the component of $G$ containing the identity element $e$. Show that $C$ is a normal subgroup of $G$.

name: exercise_26_11
formal_statement:
{X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [CompactSpace X] [T2Space X]
  (A : Set (Set X)) (hA : ∀ (a b : Set X), a ∈ A → b ∈ A → a ⊆ b ∨ b ⊆ a)
  (hA' : ∀ a ∈ A, IsClosed a) (hA'' : ∀ a ∈ A, IsConnected a) :
  IsConnected (⋂₀ A) :=
natural_language_statement: Let $X$ be a compact Hausdorff space. Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a collection of closed connected subsets of $X$ that is simply ordered by proper inclusion. Then $Y=\bigcap_{A \in \mathcal{A}} A$ is connected.

name: exercise_26_12
formal_statement:
{X Y : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y]
  (p : X → Y) (h : Function.Surjective p) (hc : Continuous p) (hp : ∀ y, IsCompact (p ⁻¹' {y}))
  (hY : CompactSpace Y) : CompactSpace X :=
natural_language_statement: Let $p: X \rightarrow Y$ be a closed continuous surjective map such that $p^{-1}(\{y\})$ is compact, for each $y \in Y$. (Such a map is called a perfect map.) Show that if $Y$ is compact, then $X$ is compact.

name: exercise_27_4
formal_statement:
{X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] [ConnectedSpace X] (hX : ∃ x y : X, x ≠ y) :
  ¬ Countable (univ : Set X) :=
natural_language_statement: Show that a connected metric space having more than one point is uncountable.

name: exercise_28_4
natural_language_statement: A space $X$ is said to be countably compact if every countable open covering of $X$ contains a finite subcollection that covers $X$. Show that for a $T_1$ space $X$, countable compactness is equivalent to limit point compactness.

name: exercise_28_5
formal_statement:
(X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] :
  countably_compact X ↔ ∀ (C : ℕ → Set X), (∀ n, IsClosed (C n)) ∧
  (∀ n, C n ≠ ∅) ∧ (∀ n, C n ⊆ C (n + 1)) → ∃ x, ∀ n, x ∈ C n :=
natural_language_statement: Show that X is countably compact if and only if every nested sequence $C_1 \supset C_2 \supset \cdots$ of closed nonempty sets of X has a nonempty intersection.

name: exercise_28_6
formal_statement:
{X : Type*} [MetricSpace X]
  [CompactSpace X] {f : X → X} (hf : Isometry f) :
  Function.Bijective f :=
natural_language_statement: Let $(X, d)$ be a metric space. If $f: X \rightarrow X$ satisfies the condition $d(f(x), f(y))=d(x, y)$ for all $x, y \in X$, then $f$ is called an isometry of $X$. Show that if $f$ is an isometry and $X$ is compact, then $f$ is bijective and hence a homeomorphism.

name: exercise_29_1
formal_statement: ¬ LocallyCompactSpace ℚ :=
natural_language_statement: Show that the rationals $\mathbb{Q}$ are not locally compact.

name: exercise_29_4
formal_statement:
[TopologicalSpace (ℕ → I)] :
  ¬ LocallyCompactSpace (ℕ → I) :=
natural_language_statement: Show that $[0, 1]^\omega$ is not locally compact in the uniform topology.

name: exercise_29_10
formal_statement:
{X : Type*}
  [TopologicalSpace X] [T2Space X] (x : X)
  (hx : ∃ U : Set X, x ∈ U ∧ IsOpen U ∧ (∃ K : Set X, U ⊂ K ∧ IsCompact K))
  (U : Set X) (hU : IsOpen U) (hxU : x ∈ U) :
  ∃ (V : Set X), IsOpen V ∧ x ∈ V ∧ IsCompact (closure V) ∧ closure V ⊆ U :=
natural_language_statement: Show that if $X$ is a Hausdorff space that is locally compact at the point $x$, then for each neighborhood $U$ of $x$, there is a neighborhood $V$ of $x$ such that $\bar{V}$ is compact and $\bar{V} \subset U$.

name: exercise_30_10
formal_statement:
{X : ℕ → Type*} [∀ i, TopologicalSpace (X i)]
  (h : ∀ i, ∃ (s : Set (X i)), Countable s ∧ Dense s) :
  ∃ (s : Set (Π i, X i)), Countable s ∧ Dense s :=
natural_language_statement: Show that if $X$ is a countable product of spaces having countable dense subsets, then $X$ has a countable dense subset.

name: exercise_30_13
formal_statement:
{X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X]
  (h : ∃ (s : Set X), Countable s ∧ Dense s) (U : Set (Set X))
  (hU : ∀ (x y : Set X), x ∈ U → y ∈ U → x ≠ y → x ∩ y = ∅) :
  Countable U :=
natural_language_statement: Show that if $X$ has a countable dense subset, every collection of disjoint open sets in $X$ is countable.

name: exercise_31_1
formal_statement:
{X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X]
  (hX : RegularSpace X) (x y : X) :
  ∃ (U V : Set X), IsOpen U ∧ IsOpen V ∧ x ∈ U ∧ y ∈ V ∧ closure U ∩ closure V = ∅ :=
natural_language_statement: Show that if $X$ is regular, every pair of points of $X$ have neighborhoods whose closures are disjoint.

name: exercise_31_2
natural_language_statement: Show that if $X$ is normal, every pair of disjoint closed sets have neighborhoods whose closures are disjoint.

name: exercise_31_3
formal_statement:
{α : Type*} [PartialOrder α]
  [TopologicalSpace α] (h : OrderTopology α) : RegularSpace α :=
natural_language_statement: Show that every order topology is regular.

name: exercise_32_1
formal_statement:
{X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X]
  (hX : NormalSpace X) (A : Set X) (hA : IsClosed A) :
  NormalSpace {x // x ∈ A} :=
natural_language_statement: Show that a closed subspace of a normal space is normal.

name: exercise_32_2a
formal_statement:
{ι : Type*} {X : ι → Type*} [∀ i, TopologicalSpace (X i)]
  (h : ∀ i, Nonempty (X i)) (h2 : T2Space (Π i, X i)) :
  ∀ i, T2Space (X i) :=
natural_language_statement: Show that if $\prod X_\alpha$ is Hausdorff, then so is $X_\alpha$. Assume that each $X_\alpha$ is nonempty.

name: exercise_32_2b
formal_statement:
{ι : Type*} {X : ι → Type*} [∀ i, TopologicalSpace (X i)]
  (h : ∀ i, Nonempty (X i)) (h2 : RegularSpace (Π i, X i)) :
  ∀ i, RegularSpace (X i) :=
natural_language_statement: Show that if $\prod X_\alpha$ is regular, then so is $X_\alpha$. Assume that each $X_\alpha$ is nonempty.

name: exercise_32_2c
formal_statement:
{ι : Type*} {X : ι → Type*} [∀ i, TopologicalSpace (X i)]
  (h : ∀ i, Nonempty (X i)) (h2 : NormalSpace (Π i, X i)) :
  ∀ i, NormalSpace (X i) :=
natural_language_statement: Show that if $\prod X_\alpha$ is normal, then so is $X_\alpha$. Assume that each $X_\alpha$ is nonempty.

name: exercise_32_3
formal_statement:
{X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X]
  (hX : LocallyCompactSpace X) (hX' : T2Space X) :
  RegularSpace X :=
